title: 15. System Design Case Studies: Design Google Drive
summary: Design Google Drive — a cloud file-storage and synchronization service with ~1 B users, ~1 TB free tier + paid upgrades, supporting file upload/download, cross-device sync, sharing with permissions, version history, and…

sections.title: Step 1: Clarify Requirements (5 min)
sections.body:
> **In one line:** Design Google Drive — a cloud file-storage and synchronization service with ~1 B users, ~1 TB free tier + paid upgrades, supporting file upload/download, cross-device sync, sharing with permissions, version history, and offline edits with conflict resolution. Focus on **chunked / resumable uploads**, **block-level deduplication**, **conflict resolution (last-writer-wins vs operational transforms)**, and the **sync notification protocol**. ---

### Functional Requirements
- **Upload / download**: files up to 5 TB (Google's actual limit), any binary type. Free tier 15 GB, paid up to 30 TB.
- **Sync**: a file edited on one device should appear on all other devices within seconds. Files of any size, with millions of files per user possible.
- **Folder hierarchy**: nested folders, rename, move, delete (moves to Trash, recoverable for 30 days, then permanently deleted).
- **Sharing**: share a file or folder with specific users (view / comment / edit) or "anyone with the link" (view / edit). Owner can revoke.
- **Version history**: keep up to 100 versions or 30 days; user can restore any prior version. For Google Docs/Sheets/Slides, revisions are infinite.
- **Offline edits**: user can edit offline; changes sync when reconnected, with conflict handling.
- **Search**: by filename, content (OCR for images, full-text for PDFs/Docs), file type, owner, modification date.
- **Real-time collaboration** for Google Docs/Sheets/Slides: multiple users editing simultaneously — out of scope (covered in collaborative editing design).
- **Comments + suggestions** for shared docs.

### Non-Functional Requirements
- **Availability** 99.99 % for metadata, 99.9 % for file blobs (blobs can fall back to multi-region S3 / Colossus).
- **Latency**: file list p99 < 200 ms, small file upload p99 < 2 s, sync notification < 5 s propagation.
- **Scale**: 1 B users, ~5 B files, ~10 EB total stored, ~1 M concurrent uploads at peak, ~10 M sync events/day.
- **Durability**: 11 nines for blobs (Colossus erasure coding + multi-region replication).
- **Security**: encryption at rest (AES-256), in transit (TLS 1.3), per-file ACLs, customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) for enterprise.

### Back-of-Envelope Estimation
- **Storage**: 1 B users × avg 100 GB used = 100 EB total. But with deduplication (~30 % savings from common OS files, app binaries, shared docs) → ~70 EB actual.
- **Metadata**: 5 B files × 1 KB metadata = 5 TB (fits in a sharded Spanner / Postgres cluster).
- **Uploads**: 1 M concurrent × 5 MB/s avg = 5 Tbps upload bandwidth globally.
- **Downloads**: 10× uploads = 50 Tbps egress.
- **Sync events**: 10 M/day × 100 notifications (one per device per user) = 1 B push notifications/day ≈ 12 k/s avg.
- **Block storage**: 4 MB block size → 100 EB / 4 MB = 25 trillion blocks. Block index (hash → blob location) at 32 bytes per entry = 800 TB.

### Scope
In scope: upload/download, sync, sharing, version history, offline edits, conflict resolution, search. Out of scope: real-time collaborative editing (separate design), Google Workspace integration, ML features (Smart Compose, Priority files).

sections.title: Step 2: High-Level Architecture (10 min)
sections.body:
### Components 1. **Client apps** (web, Android, iOS, desktop): handle local file watching (FSEvents / inotify / ReadDirectoryChangesW), chunking, encryption, sync queue. 2. **Edge / CDN**: cache public file thumbnails and shared-link previews. 3. **API Gateway** (Envoy): OAuth 2.0 auth, rate limiting, request routing. 4. **Metadata Service**: manages file/folder tree, ACLs, version pointers. Backed by Spanner (Google) / CockroachDB for global consistency. 5. **Block Service**: handles chunked uploads (resumable), block-level dedup via SHA-256 hash, stores blocks in Colossus / S3. 6. **Sync Service**: maintains per-user event log (LSN — log sequence number), notifies all devices of changes. 7. **Notification Service**: pushes "new changes available" to devices via FCM (Android), APNs (iOS), WebSocket (web/desktop). 8. **Search Service**: Elasticsearch over file metadata + extracted text (OCR, PDF parsing). 9. **Permission Service**: ACL checks (owner, editor, commenter, viewer) for every file/folder access. 10. **Thumbnail / Preview Service**: generates thumbnails (image, video, PDF preview) lazily on first access. 11. **Storage layer**: Colossus (Google's distributed file system) or S3 for blobs; Spanner for metadata; Redis for hot metadata cache. ### Mermaid Diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD Client[Desktop / Mobile / Web Client] --> GW[API Gateway
OAuth2 + rate-limit] GW --> MS[Metadata Service] GW --> BS[Block Service
chunked upload, dedup] GW --> SS[Sync Service
per-user event log] GW --> PS[Permission Service] GW --> SR[Search Service] MS --> SP[(Spanner: files,
folders, ACLs,
versions)] MS --> RC[(Redis: hot metadata)] BS --> BI[(Block Index:
SHA256 -> blob)] BS --> COL[(Colossus / S3:
4MB blocks)] SS --> LOG[(Event Log:
per-user LSN)] SS --> NS[Notification Service] NS --> FCM[FCM / APNs /
WebSocket] SR --> ES[(Elasticsearch:
filename + content)] PS --> SP Client <-. changes .-> NS style BS fill:#ffe4b5 style SS fill:#b5ffe4 style COL fill:#ffd5d5 ``` ### ASCII Diagram ``` +-----------+ +-----------+ +-----------+ | Desktop / | | Edge | | API | | Mobile / |----->| CDN |----->| Gateway | | Web App | +-----------+ +-----+-----+ +-----+-----+ | | local file watcher (FSEvents/inotify)| | chunk + encrypt + hash | | v | +------------------------------+----------+ | | | | | | v v v v | +----------+ +----------+ +---------+ +---------+ | | Metadata | | Block | | Sync | | Search | | | Service | | Service | | Service | | Service | | +----+-----+ +----+-----+ +----+----+ +----+----+ | | | | | | v v v v | +----------+ +----------+ +---------+ +---------+ | | Spanner | | Block | | Event | | Elastic | | | files, | | Index | | Log | | search | | | folders, | | (hash-> | | (per- | | index | | | ACLs, | | blob) | | user) | | | | | versions | +----+-----+ +----+----+ +---------+ | +----------+ | | | v v | +----------+ +-----------+ | | Colossus | | Notify | | | / S3 | | Service | | | 4MB blocks| +-----+-----+ | +----------+ | | v +<----- change notification ---- FCM/APNs/WebSocket ``` ### Request Flow Walkthrough 1. **Upload (large file, e.g., 1 GB video)**: Client computes file hash → splits into 4 MB chunks → for each chunk, computes SHA-256 → calls `POST /blocks/check` with hashes → Block Service returns list of missing hashes → client uploads only missing chunks via resumable PUT → Block Service verifies hash, stores in Colossus, updates Block Index → client calls `POST /files` with the list of block hashes + metadata → Metadata Service creates the file row, links blocks, increments user's quota. 2. **Sync (file modified on laptop)**: Client detects inotify event → re-chunks the changed portion (block-level diff) → uploads only changed blocks → calls `POST /files/{id}/commit` with new version + block list → Sync Service appends to the user's event log → Notification Service pushes "LSN=42" to all other devices → other devices call `GET /sync/changes?since_lsn=41` to fetch the diff. 3. **Offline conflict**: User edits offline on phone for 2 hours, comes back online → client commits → server detects the same file was modified by another device in the meantime → conflict resolver applies last-writer-wins for plain files (preserving both versions) or operational transform for Google Docs → both versions retained in history.

sections.title: Step 3: Deep Dive — Data Model (10 min)
sections.body:
### Tables / Schema

**Spanner — `files`** (one row per file version)
```sql
CREATE TABLE files (
    file_id         STRING(36),       -- UUID
    parent_folder_id STRING(36),
    owner_id        INT64,
    name            STRING(255),
    is_folder       BOOL,
    size_bytes      INT64,
    mime_type       STRING(100),
    version         INT64,            -- incremented per edit
    block_list      ARRAY<STRING>,    -- list of block hashes
    created_at      TIMESTAMP,
    modified_at     TIMESTAMP,
    deleted_at      TIMESTAMP,        -- null unless trashed
) PRIMARY KEY (file_id, version);
```

**Spanner — `acl_entries`** (per-file permissions)
```sql
CREATE TABLE acl_entries (
    file_id     STRING(36),
    principal   STRING(64),     -- user_id, group_id, or "anyone-with-link"
    role        STRING(16),     -- owner | editor | commenter | viewer
    granted_at  TIMESTAMP,
    granted_by  INT64,
) PRIMARY KEY (file_id, principal);
```

**Spanner — `block_index`** (dedup index; billions of rows)
```sql
CREATE TABLE block_index (
    block_hash    STRING(64),     -- SHA-256 hex
    size_bytes    INT64,
    storage_location STRING(128), -- e.g., colossus://path or s3://bucket/key
    ref_count     INT64,          -- how many files reference this block
    first_seen    TIMESTAMP,
) PRIMARY KEY (block_hash);
```

**Spanner — `user_event_log`** (per-user change log)
```sql
CREATE TABLE user_event_log (
    user_id    INT64,
    lsn        INT64,             -- log sequence number, monotonic
    event_type STRING(32),        -- file_created | file_modified | file_deleted | acl_changed
    file_id    STRING(36),
    version    INT64,
    payload    BYTES,             -- JSON-serialized event details
    ts         TIMESTAMP,
) PRIMARY KEY (user_id, lsn);
```

**Spanner — `user_quota`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE user_quota (
    user_id        INT64 PRIMARY KEY,
    plan           STRING(16),    -- free | 100gb | 2tb | 30tb
    bytes_used     INT64,
    bytes_limit    INT64,
);
```

### Indexes
- `files (parent_folder_id, name)` — folder listing (children of a folder).
- `files (owner_id, modified_at DESC)` — "My Drive" recent files.
- `acl_entries (file_id, principal)` — permission check.
- `block_index (block_hash)` — dedup lookup (primary key).
- `user_event_log (user_id, lsn)` — sync delta query.

### Storage Choice
- **Spanner** (or CockroachDB / YugabyteDB outside Google): globally distributed, externally consistent ACID transactions, perfect for file metadata + ACLs where a half-committed rename is a bug. Spanner's TrueTime gives linearizability across regions.
- **Colossus** (Google's distributed file system, successor to GFS) or **S3** for block blobs: 11-nines durability via erasure coding + multi-region replication, ~$0.026/GB-month for S3 Standard, lifecycle to Glacier for cold files.
- **Block Index** in Spanner (or a dedicated KV store like Bigtable for higher write throughput): hash → blob location lookup must be O(1) and globally consistent to dedup correctly.
- **Redis** for hot metadata cache (recent file lists, ACL checks) — sub-ms reads.
- **Elasticsearch** for search over filenames + extracted text content.

sections.title: Step 4: Deep Dive — Key Algorithms & APIs (10 min)
sections.body:
### API Design
```
# Resumable, chunked, dedup-aware upload

POST /api/v1/uploads/init
  body: { "filename": "video.mp4", "size_bytes": 1073741824,
          "mime_type": "video/mp4", "parent_folder_id": "..." }
  resp: { "upload_id": "...", "block_size": 4194304,
          "num_blocks": 256 }

POST /api/v1/uploads/{upload_id}/check-blocks
  body: { "hashes": ["sha256:abc...", "sha256:def...", ...] }
  resp: { "missing": ["sha256:def...", "sha256:ghi..."] }

PUT  /api/v1/uploads/{upload_id}/blocks/{block_hash}
  headers: Content-Range: bytes 0-4194303/*
  body: <4 MB raw bytes>
  resp: { "stored": true, "already_existed": false }

POST /api/v1/files
  body: { "filename": "...", "parent_folder_id": "...",
          "block_hashes": ["sha256:abc...", ...],
          "mime_type": "video/mp4", "size_bytes": 1073741824 }
  resp: { "file_id": "...", "version": 1 }

# Sync
GET  /api/v1/sync/changes?since_lsn=41
  resp: { "changes": [{"lsn":42,"event":"file_modified","file_id":"...","version":3}, ...],
          "latest_lsn": 45 }

POST /api/v1/files/{id}/commit
  body: { "version": 3, "block_hashes": [...], "base_version": 2 }
  resp: { "file_id": "...", "version": 3, "conflict": false }

# Sharing
POST /api/v1/files/{id}/acl
  body: { "principal": "user:alice@example.com", "role": "editor" }
DELETE /api/v1/files/{id}/acl/{principal}

# Versions
GET  /api/v1/files/{id}/versions
POST /api/v1/files/{id}/versions/{v}/restore
```

### Key Algorithms

**1. Chunked resumable upload.** A 5 TB upload cannot fit in one HTTP request — it would time out, fail mid-way with no recovery, and waste bandwidth. Design: client computes the file's block structure (4 MB blocks), then for each block: (a) compute SHA-256, (b) call `/check-blocks` with all hashes — server returns which are missing (already deduped or already uploaded in this session), (c) upload only missing blocks via `PUT /blocks/{hash}` with `Content-Range` for resumability. If the connection drops at block 47/256, the client retries only block 47 (and onwards), not the whole file. Each block PUT is idempotent (same hash → same outcome).

**2. Block-level deduplication.** When a client uploads a 1 GB PDF that's identical to one already stored for another user, the Block Service computes SHA-256 of each 4 MB chunk and looks them up in `block_index`. If a hash exists with `ref_count > 0`, the block is already stored — no need to re-upload. The client just records the hash list in the new file's metadata, and `block_index.ref_count` is incremented. This saves enormous storage for common files (OS ISOs, popular videos, shared documents). Two users uploading the same 1 GB movie = 1 GB stored, not 2 GB. Trade-off: dedup at 4 MB granularity catches more matches than file-level dedup but is more expensive to compute (one hash per 4 MB vs one per file). At Google Drive's scale, ~30 % of bytes are deduped, saving ~30 EB.

**3. Versioning.** Each `commit` creates a new row in `files` with the same `file_id` but incremented `version`. Old versions are retained (Google's actual policy: 100 versions or 30 days, whichever is more permissive; unlimited for Google Docs). Restore = copy the old version's `block_list` to a new version row. No block duplication needed — `block_index.ref_count` tracks usage across all versions.

**4. Conflict resolution (offline edits).** When two devices edit the same file offline and both commit, the server uses **revision vector clocks**: each version carries `(device_id, lamport_ts)`. On commit with `base_version = N`:
- If `base_version == current_version`: fast-path commit, increment version.
- If `base_version < current_version`: conflict. For binary files (images, PDFs), **last-writer-wins** — the later commit wins, the earlier is preserved as a prior version. For Google Docs (text), **operational transform (OT)** or **CRDTs** merge the edits non-destructively. For folders (rename / move), detect rename-vs-rename conflicts and prompt the user.
- The `conflict` flag in the response tells the client to fetch and merge.

**5. Sync notification protocol.** Each user has an `event_log` keyed by `(user_id, lsn)`. When a file is modified, the Sync Service appends an event with the next LSN, then pushes a "wake up, LSN=42" notification via FCM/APNs/WebSocket to all the user's other devices. Each device maintains its `last_seen_lsn` locally and calls `GET /sync/changes?since_lsn={last_seen}` to fetch deltas. This is a **pull-on-push** model — the notification is just a trigger; the actual data is pulled, which scales better than pushing full payloads. Long-polling fallback for clients without push.

**6. Permission check.** Every file/folder access goes through the Permission Service: `can(user_id, file_id, action)` walks the folder tree up to the root, checking `acl_entries` at each level (ACLs inherit from parent folders). Result cached in Redis for 60 s with `acl:{user_id}:{file_id}:{action}` → `bool`. On ACL change, invalidate the cache for that file and all descendants (cascade).

**7. Thumbnail / preview generation.** On first access to a file, if no thumbnail exists, the Metadata Service enqueues a job to the Thumbnail Service (image: resize with Pillow; video: FFmpeg extract frame at 1 s; PDF: pdftoppm first page; DOC: headless Chrome render). Result stored in Colossus at `thumbnails/{file_id}/{version}.jpg`, cached at CDN for 1 hour.

```python
# google_drive_sync.py — chunked upload, block-level dedup, conflict detection
import hashlib, threading, time
from collections import defaultdict

BLOCK_SIZE = 4 * 1024 * 1024   # 4 MB

def sha256(b): return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()

class ColossusMock:
    """Block-level storage with dedup index."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.blocks = {}              # hash -> bytes
        self.ref_count = defaultdict(int)
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
    def has(self, h): return h in self.blocks
    def put(self, h, data):
        with self.lock:
            if h in self.blocks:
                self.ref_count[h] += 1
                return False   # already existed
            self.blocks[h] = data
            self.ref_count[h] = 1
            return True
    def get(self, h): return self.blocks.get(h)
    def delete(self, h):
        with self.lock:
            self.ref_count[h] -= 1
            if self.ref_count[h] == 0:
                del self.blocks[h]; del self.ref_count[h]

class SpannerMock:
    """Metadata: files, versions, ACLs, event log."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.files = {}               # file_id -> {name, owner, versions: [v1, v2, ...]}
        self.acl = defaultdict(dict)  # file_id -> {principal: role}
        self.event_log = defaultdict(list)  # user_id -> [event, ...]
        self.lsn = defaultdict(int)
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
    def create_file(self, file_id, owner, name, block_hashes, size):
        v1 = {"version": 1, "blocks": block_hashes, "size": size,
              "ts": time.time(), "author_device": "init"}
        self.files[file_id] = {"name": name, "owner": owner,
                                "versions": [v1], "parent": None}
        self.acl[file_id][f"user:{owner}"] = "owner"
        self._append_event(owner, "file_created", file_id, 1)
        return 1
    def commit_version(self, file_id, owner, block_hashes, size,
                       base_version, device_id):
        with self.lock:
            f = self.files[file_id]
            current = f["versions"][-1]["version"]
            if base_version != current:
                # conflict: last-writer-wins, preserve old as version
                print(f"  [conflict] base={base_version} current={current} -> LWW")
                new_v = current + 1
                f["versions"].append({"version": new_v, "blocks": block_hashes,
                                       "size": size, "ts": time.time(),
                                       "author_device": device_id, "conflict": True})
                self._append_event(owner, "file_modified_conflict", file_id, new_v)
                return new_v, True
            new_v = current + 1
            f["versions"].append({"version": new_v, "blocks": block_hashes,
                                   "size": size, "ts": time.time(),
                                   "author_device": device_id})
            self._append_event(owner, "file_modified", file_id, new_v)
            return new_v, False
    def _append_event(self, user_id, ev_type, file_id, version):
        self.lsn[user_id] += 1
        self.event_log[user_id].append({"lsn": self.lsn[user_id],
                                         "type": ev_type, "file_id": file_id,
                                         "version": version, "ts": time.time()})
    def get_changes(self, user_id, since_lsn):
        return [e for e in self.event_log[user_id] if e["lsn"] > since_lsn]

class BlockService:
    def __init__(self, colossus): self.c = colossus
    def check_blocks(self, hashes):
        return [h for h in hashes if not self.c.has(h)]
    def upload_block(self, h, data):
        return self.c.put(h, data)

class SyncService:
    def __init__(self, spanner): self.s = spanner
    def commit(self, file_id, owner, name, block_hashes, size, base_version, device_id):
        if base_version == 0:
            return self.s.create_file(file_id, owner, name, block_hashes, size), False
        return self.s.commit_version(file_id, owner, block_hashes, size,
                                      base_version, device_id)
    def pull(self, user_id, since_lsn):
        return self.s.get_changes(user_id, since_lsn)

class DriveClient:
    """Simulates the desktop/mobile client."""
    def __init__(self, block_svc, sync_svc, device_id):
        self.b = block_svc; self.s = sync_svc; self.device = device_id
        self.last_lsn = 0
    def upload_file(self, file_id, owner, name, data):
        # 1. chunk + hash
        blocks = []
        for i in range(0, len(data), BLOCK_SIZE):
            chunk = data[i:i+BLOCK_SIZE]
            blocks.append((sha256(chunk), chunk))
        # 2. dedup check
        missing = self.b.check_blocks([h for h, _ in blocks])
        print(f"  [{self.device}] upload {name}: {len(blocks)} blocks, "
              f"{len(missing)} missing (dedup saved {len(blocks)-len(missing)})")
        # 3. upload missing
        for h, chunk in blocks:
            if h in missing:
                self.b.upload_block(h, chunk)
        return [h for h, _ in blocks]
    def commit(self, file_id, owner, name, block_hashes, size, base_version=None):
        v, conflict = self.s.commit(file_id, owner, name, block_hashes, size,
                                     base_version or 0, self.device)
        print(f"  [{self.device}] committed {name} v{v} conflict={conflict}")
        return v, conflict
    def sync(self, user_id):
        changes = self.s.pull(user_id, self.last_lsn)
        if changes:
            self.last_lsn = changes[-1]["lsn"]
            print(f"  [{self.device}] synced {len(changes)} changes "
                  f"(now at LSN {self.last_lsn})")
        return changes

if __name__ == "__main__":
    colossus = ColossusMock()
    spanner = SpannerMock()
    block_svc = BlockService(colossus)
    sync_svc = SyncService(spanner)

    alice = 1
    # Alice's laptop uploads a 12 MB PDF (3 blocks of 4MB, each different content)
    laptop = DriveClient(block_svc, sync_svc, "laptop")
    pdf_data = b"A" * BLOCK_SIZE + b"B" * BLOCK_SIZE + b"C" * BLOCK_SIZE
    hashes = laptop.upload_file("file-1", alice, "doc.pdf", pdf_data)
    laptop.commit("file-1", alice, "doc.pdf", hashes, len(pdf_data), base_version=0)

    # Alice's phone also has the same PDF — should dedup completely
    phone = DriveClient(block_svc, sync_svc, "phone")
    hashes2 = phone.upload_file("file-2", alice, "copy.pdf", pdf_data)
    phone.commit("file-2", alice, "copy.pdf", hashes2, len(pdf_data), base_version=0)
    print(f"  [dedup] Colossus stored {len(colossus.blocks)} unique blocks "
          f"(should be 3, not 6)")

    # Phone modifies the file (block 2 changes) - delta upload
    print("\n[Phone edits block 2]")
    new_data = b"A" * BLOCK_SIZE + b"B" * BLOCK_SIZE + b"X" * BLOCK_SIZE
    new_hashes = []
    for i in range(0, len(new_data), BLOCK_SIZE):
        new_hashes.append(sha256(new_data[i:i+BLOCK_SIZE]))
    missing = block_svc.check_blocks(new_hashes)
    print(f"  [delta] only {len(missing)} of {len(new_hashes)} blocks need upload")
    for i, h in enumerate(new_hashes):
        if h in missing:
            block_svc.upload_block(h, new_data[i*BLOCK_SIZE:(i+1)*BLOCK_SIZE])
    sync_svc.commit("file-1", alice, "doc.pdf", new_hashes, len(new_data),
                     base_version=1, device_id="phone")
    print(f"  [after edit] file-1 has {len(spanner.files['file-1']['versions'])} versions, "
          f"Colossus has {len(colossus.blocks)} unique blocks")

    # Conflict: both devices try to commit from base_version=1
    print("\n[Conflict scenario: both devices edit offline from v1]")
    v2_data = b"X" * (BLOCK_SIZE * 3)
    v2_hashes = [sha256(v2_data[i:i+BLOCK_SIZE]) for i in range(0, len(v2_data), BLOCK_SIZE)]
    v3_data = b"Y" * (BLOCK_SIZE * 3)
    v3_hashes = [sha256(v3_data[i:i+BLOCK_SIZE]) for i in range(0, len(v3_data), BLOCK_SIZE)]
    # Both base off version 1
    sync_svc.commit("file-1", alice, "doc.pdf", v2_hashes, len(v2_data),
                     base_version=1, device_id="laptop")
    sync_svc.commit("file-1", alice, "doc.pdf", v3_hashes, len(v3_data),
                     base_version=1, device_id="phone")  # conflict
    print(f"  [versions] file-1 now has {len(spanner.files['file-1']['versions'])} versions")

    # Sync pulls
    print("\n[Sync]")
    laptop.sync(alice)
    phone.sync(alice)
```

Running this shows: full dedup (3 blocks stored, not 6), delta upload (1 of 3 blocks), conflict detection (last-writer-wins, version preserved), and sync pull (devices converge to latest LSN).

sections.title: Step 5: Scalability & Reliability (5 min)
sections.body:
### Scaling Challenges
- **Block index hot spots**: a globally shared file (e.g., Windows ISO) causes a hot block hash — every check lookup hits one Spanner row. Mitigation: cache positive results in Redis (TTL 1 h); use a dedicated Bigtable cluster for the block index (better write throughput than Spanner for this access pattern).
- **Upload bandwidth**: 1 M concurrent uploads at 5 MB/s = 5 Tbps. Mitigation: geo-distributed ingest points (Google Front Ends in 100+ POPs), per-region Colossus clusters, async replication between regions.
- **Spanner hot shards**: a single user with millions of files hits one Spanner tablet. Mitigation: Spanner auto-splits tablets at ~4 GB; interleave `files` and `acl_entries` on `file_id` for locality.
- **Sync fan-out**: one file change → notify all of the user's devices (avg 3). With 10 M file changes/day × 3 devices = 30 M notifications/day. FCM/APNs handle this easily; WebSocket connections require sharded connection servers (like WhatsApp's connection layer).
- **Quota enforcement**: must be atomic with file commit — a user could otherwise upload unlimited data by racing commits. Mitigation: Spanner transaction wraps `INSERT file` + `UPDATE user_quota.bytes_used` + check `bytes_used + new_size <= bytes_limit`.
- **Search index lag**: Elasticsearch indexing of new files lags by 1–5 s. For "recently uploaded" searches, fall back to Spanner `ORDER BY created_at DESC`.

### Caching Strategy
- **L1 (client)**: local file metadata cache (SQLite) for instant folder listing even offline.
- **L2 (Redis)**: hot folder listings (children of `/My Drive`, `/Shared with me`) cached 60 s; ACL decisions cached 60 s.
- **L3 (Spanner)**: source of truth.
- **CDN**: thumbnails and shared-link previews cached 1 h at edge.

### Failure Modes
- **Colossus / S3 outage**: uploads fail with 5xx; client retries with exponential backoff. Reads of already-cached blocks succeed; new block reads fail. Multi-region failover for blobs (S3 cross-region replication, Colossus DC replication).
- **Spanner split-brain**: extremely rare due to Paxos + TrueTime, but if a partition occurs, the minority side rejects writes (no stale reads) until healed.
- **Notification service down**: clients fall back to polling (`GET /sync/changes?since_lsn=N`) every 30 s. Higher load but functional.
- **Client clock skew**: Lamport timestamps for version vectors don't depend on wall-clock; only the display "modified 5 min ago" can be wrong.
- **Dedup hash collision**: SHA-256 collisions are computationally infeasible (~2^128 brute force), but for paranoia we can also store the block size and verify on read.

quiz.question: Why does Google Drive use 4 MB blocks instead of file-level dedup?
options: Pure server-push of full file payloads is infeasible (3 B devices × per-change payload = exabytes/day).
This is a "ghost file" incident — the metadata and the user's view are inconsistent.
Downloading 1 GB at 100 KB/s takes ~3 hours — too slow, and any interruption restarts from scratch.
File-level dedup only catches identical whole files — two users uploading the same Windows ISO.
quiz.explanation: File-level dedup only catches identical whole files — two users uploading the same Windows ISO. But many real cases involve files that share most blocks but differ slightly: a PowerPoint template filled in by 1 000 different users (each slide deck is 99 % identical template, 1 % unique content), an OS image with one config changed, a large video re-encoded with one extra second.

quiz.explanation: A 5 TB upload at 100 MB/s takes ~14 hours — network interruptions are guaranteed. The protocol: (1) Client calls POST /uploads/init to get an upload_id (valid for 7 days). (2) Client splits the file into 4 MB blocks, computes SHA-256 of each.

quiz.explanation: Pure server-push of full file payloads is infeasible (3 B devices × per-change payload = exabytes/day). The design is pull-on-push: (1) Each device maintains a long-lived connection to a Notification Service (WebSocket for web/desktop, FCM for Android, APNs for iOS).

This is a real concern: a "confirmation of existence" attack.
quiz.explanation: This is a real concern: a "confirmation of existence" attack. If an attacker can check whether a specific hash exists in the Block Index, they can confirm whether a target user has a particular file (e.g., a known sensitive document). Mitigations: (1) Hash check requires auth: POST /check-blocks requires a valid user OAuth token; the server only returns missing hashes that the caller has upload rights to.
